newsitem.title: USA: Giuliani: kidnappers may have selected deaf-mutes.
newsitem.headline: Giuliani: kidnappers may have selected deaf-mutes.

text.p: Seven people have been arrested in a bizarre case involving more than 60 Mexicans, most of whom were deaf and mute, who were rescued by authorities after months of forced servitude selling trinkets on the street, police said on Sunday.

"The people involved in this scheme of holding these Mexicans in bondage and in virtual slavery selected people who were deaf and mute so that they would be in more fear in this country," Mayor Rudolph Giuliani told a Sunday news conference.

The Immigration and Naturalisation Service placed a detainer on the Mexicans but Giuliani said he put a stop to that by placing them all in the custody of New York City authorities. He said the American Red Cross was providing them with housing and food "until we know their correct status" in this country.

"We have to make sure that enough of them remain here so that the cases can be properly prosecuted because these people are witnesses and will have to testify against the people responsible for this," the mayor said.
The mayor said that there are indications that the Mexicans were kidnapped and smuggled into the United States.

Giuliani said some of the Mexicans may have been here for years. At least two told the mayor they knew him because they have pictures taken with him at an Ecuadorian parade a few years ago. "That indicates they have been here quite some time," he said.

Four of those arrested faced federal charges of smuggling, harbouring and transporting aliens and conspiracy, while the other three faced state charges including coercion, grand larceny, harassment and assault, police said.
Police said that Alfredo Rustrian-Paoletti, 37, was evidently the leader. He was the first taken in for questioning on Saturday and now faces the federal charges.

The others were picked up throughout Saturday after four of the deaf and mute Mexicans walked into a police station in Jackson Heights, in the New York City borough of Queens early Saturday seeking help. In sign language they told a bizarre story of being held captive with the other handicapped Mexicans by a man who forced them to sell trinkets for pittance wages.
Police went to two locations described by the four men and rescued 58 other men, women and children. It was not clear how long the Mexicans had been captive, police said.
Forty-four people were found at the first location and 18 at the second site. Giuliani said $30,000 in cash was recovered at one of the locations.
Police said the Mexicans were living in two-family attached homes designed to house seven or eight people. "They were living on mattresses on the floor," police said.

The other three facing federal charges are Jose Paoletti, 26, Rufegia Santa, 21, Rosa Betran Sanchez, 26. Arrested on state charges are Adriana Paoletti, 29, for coercion and grand larceny, Delia Paoletti, 67, for coercion and harassment, and Raul Alanis, 24, for coercion and assault.
Of the 62 Mexicans rescued by police, 30 were women and 10 were children. The mayor indicated there may be more Mexicans being held at other locations.

The deaf and mute Mexicans had told police they were brought here from Mexico and were made to work the streets of Manhattan, Queens and New Jersey peddling trinkets such as key chains, pens and toys.
